title: render: honour a realm's rule_identifier_format
description: entity.RealmFile.RuleIdentifierFormat is documented as overriding the RLIFRMT rule-ID rendering defaults, but nothing reads it: it is an untyped interface{}, and render.MarkdownRenderer always uses DefaultRuleIDFormatter (its formatter field is unexported, and the only Option is WithTemplate). A realm that sets rule_identifier_format is therefore ignored without any warning. Found via Copilot review on PR #128.
design: 1) Give RealmFile.RuleIdentifierFormat a concrete type (open/close bracket, revision/state splitter) matching the realm.v1 schema and the RLIFRMT rules in strspc-rules core. 2) Add render.WithRuleIDFormatter(RuleIDFormatter) Option and a helper building a formatter from the realm setting, with unset fields falling back to the RLIFRMT defaults. 3) Optionally have realmlint validate the field. Callers (strspc-CLI render) pass the realm's setting through.
acceptance_criteria: Rendering an entity of a realm with rule_identifier_format uses that format; unset fields fall back to the defaults; README render row and SPEC updated; tests cover override and fallback.
notes:
Blocked upstream (decision 2026-10-28: upstream first, wait): SteerSpec/strspc-rules#78 must define the rule_identifier_format object in realm.v1 and release it. Related: strspc-rules#55 item 5 (RLIFRMT-002/004/006/007 Implemented only via hard-coded defaults). Also strspc-CLI realm init types the field as *string. Raised to P0 by PLB.
Upstream released in strspc-rules v1.10.0. Manager PR #135 opened 2026-10-28; close on merge.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #135: typed rule_identifier_format, NewRuleIDFormatter/WithRuleIDFormatter, RM013.

title: dependencies_test.go holds the live core pin, so the next core pin PR fails
description: src/realmlint/dependencies_test.go used the repo's live core version in coreSource, which matches the pin regex in strspc-rules tools/pin_core.py. On the next core release the strspc-manager leg of pin-consumers.yml fails with a 'pins outside the file list' error naming that file, and no pin PR opens. Listing the file in the matrix is wrong: it would rewrite coreSource only, while the table keeps the old version, breaking TestRM014_SourceTag. Found by dry-running pin_core.py against a fresh clone, 2026-10-30. Fix: use a fixture version no release will hold (for example 9.9.9) in coreSource and in the versions compared with it. Do not write a literal core pin in bead text: .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked, so pin_core.py scans it too.
acceptance_criteria: pin_core.py apply --new 1.12.0 passes on a strspc-manager checkout with the docs/SPEC.md matrix list, and go test ./src/realmlint passes.
notes:
PR #160 against develop: approved, CI green, mergeStateStatus CLEAN, no Copilot findings. Close after the user merges.
Correction to the close reason: no promotion is needed. pin-consumers.yml checks out the consumer's default branch, which is develop, so the fix applies to the next pin PR now.
close_reason: Merged in PR #160 (bc04c0c on develop). Test fixtures now use 9.9.9. pin_core.py apply --new 1.12.0 with the matrix list failed before the fix and passes after, on throwaway clones. The fix reaches consumers' pin PRs only once develop is promoted to main.

title: Resolve the entity schema from the realm's pinned core version
description: schema.Fetcher reads the latest site schema and caches it forever (strspc-rules-3a8.10). Resolve from the realm instead: a dependency on dev.steerspec.core@X.Y.Z uses steerspec.dev/rules/vX.Y.Z/_schema/, immutable and safe to cache; the core realm uses its local rules/core/_schema/; no realm context or no versioned schema falls back to the latest URL with short-lived revalidation, keeping a stale copy for offline use. Acceptance: with empty and stale caches a realm pinned to 1.10.0 rejects inherits with RL002 and one pinned to 1.11.0 accepts it. strspc-CLI wires this in afterwards.
notes:
PR #159 open against develop on branch feat/realm-pinned-schema (rebased from local feat/schema-from-realm). ForRealm prefers _schema/ for every realm, then pin, then latest. realm-lint wired. Acceptance verified end-to-end. Remaining: merge, then strspc-CLI wiring.
Security review on #159: (1) FIXED ed6ccbb: both compilers load no external refs. (2) OPEN, user's decision: non-core _schema/ overrides the pin and RM015 is skipped in realm-lint (no dependency fetcher), so a tampered _schema/ passes silently. Alternative: pin first, local _schema/ for core only.
Decision taken after Copilot flagged the same issue and the user said fix: pin first for non-core realms, local _schema/ for core only (4d0d516). WithSubRealmLinters added for sub-realms with their own pin.
close_reason: Merged in #159 (cefcdae) to develop. Pinned-release resolution, TTL on latest and stale offline fallback shipped. Acceptance verified end-to-end on the normal user cache; empty and stale cache cases covered by unit tests only. strspc-CLI wiring tracked separately.

title: release-please drops develop commits dated before the last release commit on main
description: release-please walks main's history newest first and stops at the last release SHA. That history is date-ordered, so a commit merged to develop before the release PR merged sits behind the release commit, even when it reaches main in a later promotion, and is ignored. Seen in release PR #172: it considered only fe6b06e and 10ee7f6 ('Splitting 2 commits by path'), because #164, #165, #166 and #169 predate 92c5783 (#168, 2026-10-30T18:55:32Z). #164 is a visible docs entry and is missing from 1.29.0. A dropped feat or fix would be worse: it would change or suppress the version bump. Had #170 merged before #168, 1.29.0 would not have been proposed. strspc-CLI and strspc-rules use the same develop to main flow.
design: Candidates: promote before merging a release PR, so a release PR never merges while develop holds unpromoted visible commits; add that as a release PR gate in strspc-pr-review#123; use BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE in the release PR body when a drop has already happened. Verify which holds on a real release.
acceptance_criteria: The flow for merging release PRs prevents this, it is documented in the README or AGENTS.md of each repo using develop to main, and one real release includes a commit merged to develop before the previous release PR merged.
notes: The approval gate for this is tracked in strspc-pr-review#124 (bead strspc-pr-review-hyw).

title: Lint PR titles now that squash makes them the commit
description: Pull requests into develop are squashed in strspc-manager, strspc-CLI and strspc-rules, so the PR title is the commit release-please reads. lint-commits runs commitlint on branch commits only, and nothing lints the title. A non-conventional title would drop the change from the release notes and version bump without any failure. Add a PR title check, on pull_request edited as well as opened and synchronize, to all three repos or to a reusable workflow in SteerSpec/.github.
acceptance_criteria: A PR with a non-conventional title fails CI in all three repos, and fixing the title clears it without a new commit.
notes: PRs: strspc-manager#166, strspc-CLI#166, strspc-rules#97. Tested: the bad title failed pr-title in all three. After merge, add a repo ruleset requiring pr-title on develop.
close_reason: pr-title.yml lints PR titles on opened, edited, synchronize and reopened in strspc-manager, strspc-CLI and strspc-rules, and repo ruleset required-pr-title requires it on develop. Auto-approve re-evaluates after it. Tested on the PRs themselves: a bad title failed the check in all three, and fixing the title cleared it without a new commit. The test ran before the check was required, so a blocked merge was not exercised.

title: Repo merge_commit_message PR_TITLE duplicates release-please changelog entries
description: Each merge commit's body carries the PR's conventional title (merge_commit_message=PR_TITLE), so release-please counts it again alongside the branch commit. v1.28.0 listed one feature and one fix twice this way: cefcdae duplicated db426b9, and 3e468c6 duplicated 8aa0a21. strspc-CLI has the same setting and v1.26.0 of it shows the same duplicate; strspc-rules has the same setting too. The BLANK fix first recorded here is invalid: GitHub rejects MERGE_MESSAGE with BLANK (HTTP 422), and the valid combinations all put the PR title in the merge commit's subject or body, so no merge commit setting removes it. Option needing a decision: squash feature PRs into develop with the PR title as subject and a blank body, keeping a merge commit only for promotions, enforced with allowed_merge_methods in the rulesets. A squash body of COMMIT_MESSAGES would carry the branch commits' conventional lines, so it must not stay the default.
acceptance_criteria: The next release PR lists each change once.
notes:
Applied to strspc-manager, strspc-CLI and strspc-rules: squash title PR_TITLE, message BLANK, and repo rulesets merge-method-develop (squash) and merge-method-main (merge). Docs PRs open in all three. Keep open until the next release PR shows each change once.
A PR merged into main still gets a merge commit, so its conventional title counts twice, and docs is a visible changelog section. docs: correct the 1.28.0 changelog (#167) opened release PR #168 for 1.28.1 with a duplicate entry. Direct fixes on main should use chore:. #168 stays open unmerged; the next promotion will update it, and its two docs lines should be removed then.
close_reason: Release PR #172 lists #170 once, so the squash fix works. #164 is missing from that PR for a different reason, tracked separately. The 1.28.1 duplicate remains in CHANGELOG.md and the release notes.

title: realmresolve: transitive dependency resolution
description: realmresolve resolves only direct dependencies; a dependency's own dependencies are never fetched or EUID-checked. Spec decision first: are realm dependencies transitive (EUID collisions RLM-006/RR005, rule loading, cycles, diamond version conflicts, RLM-009 refs)? Then implement or document direct-only. Remaining gap of GH #9 / strspc-manager-hx6. GH #137.
notes: Inheritance (#143) already loads deps of deps when a chain reaches them, with per-hop pins, so that is a precedent for the spec decision. See the comment on GH #137.

title: Supersede MOD-002 to list the EC (evalcache) diagnostic prefix
description: MOD-002 [I] enumerates six prefixes (RL RD RM RR RSV RE) but evalcache emits EC001 (SPEC §6.3) and the MOD-002 test in PR #115 holds evalcache to EC. A Published/Implemented body is final, so use 'strspc rule supersede MOD-002 --dir rules' with the seven-prefix wording, then promote the successor D→P→I (the test already enforces it).
notes: Needs three PRs, one per state change, because rule-diff forbids skipping states: (1) strspc rule supersede MOD-002 --dir rules adds the successor (MOD-007 (MOD-006 is taken)) in D with all seven prefixes (RL, RD, RM, RR, RSV, RE, EC) and supersedes: MOD-002 (RD004: new rules start in D); (2) strspc rule promote D->P (RD003: D->I in one diff is a skip); (3) promote P->I and retire MOD-002 I->R in the same PR (RD006 warns otherwise). Each PR touches only rules/MOD.json; no Go changes, since ownedPrefix in src/result/codes_lifecycle_test.go already maps src/evalcache to EC. A clarification note is not enough: notes must not modify the rule (SPEC 2.5).
close_reason: MOD-007 Implemented, MOD-002 Retired (PRs #130, #131 and this one)

title: realmlint: option for callers that lint entity files elsewhere
description: strspc realm validate --recursive leaves realmlint's rule linter unset because rulelint.LintRealm lints the entity files, so realmlint reports info RM005 (entity file validation skipped), which is false there. strspc-CLI filters that note on code and severity (strspc-CLI#171, strspc-cli-e8h). An option such as WithEntityLintingDelegated would state this directly and stop the note at its source.
design: Do this together with strspc-cli-dla, which also needs a manager change (LintRealm taking a per-sub-realm linter), so the CLI bumps once. Not worth a release alone.
acceptance_criteria: With the option set, realmlint emits no info RM005 and RM005 errors still appear. docs/SPEC.md describes it. A strspc-CLI change uses it and removes dropSkippedEntityNotes.
